purpose: The exact, per-entry disposition of the five Super Administrator contract pages that stay disabled_by_gate. It exists because a single shared gate label would tell an operator that all five are waiting on the same decision, when three of them are waiting on a PHASE that is waiting on that decision. Each row names the dependency that actually blocks it, who owns the backend, and the condition that would open it.
invariants: No gated entry has a registered runtime route, an href, or a router destination in any placement.
No gated entry names a component, a store, or an API operation.
No gated metric is rendered as zero, healthy, empty, complete or up to date.
Each entry is visible and keyboard reachable so its reason can be read; it is inert, not hidden.

No client-supplied input can open a gate. `NavigationContext` carries no gate override (UI08-NAV-002); a gate opens only by the canonical map being regenerated with implementation_status: implemented.

placements: nav-overflow-gated-{key} — the 'More' overflow disclosure below xl
nav-stacked-gated-{key} — the mobile drawer's always-open sections
runtime_treatment.semantics: role-less span with aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="0", carrying a visible reason; never an anchor, never a button that routes

entries.title: Billing Reconciliation Exceptions
entries.blocked_by: External Gate W — Wallet by Citrus collections readiness (Plan §80.2)
entries.entry_condition: External Gate W opens (docs/integrations/wallet/gate-w-evidence.md exists and is accepted), Phase 20D-W ships the exception queue, and both permission keys become implementation_status: active.
entries.why_no_partial_page: Servana holds no Wallet-confirmed money-movement records, so there is no exception to list and no allocation to preview. A queue rendered empty would assert that reconciliation is clean.
entries.ownership_boundary: Wallet by Citrus owns provider credentials, callbacks, settlement and money-movement truth. Servana never creates a manual payment path.

entries.title: Integrations Health
entries.blocked_by: External Gate W — Wallet by Citrus collections readiness (Plan §80.2)
entries.entry_condition: External Gate W opens and Phase 20D-W ships Wallet client health, circuit-breaker state, webhook verification and inbox telemetry. Phase 21R-A explicitly deferred this screen to 20D-W.
entries.why_no_partial_page: No Wallet client health, latency, circuit-breaker or webhook telemetry exists. A green health indicator derived from the absence of data is a fabricated assurance.
entries.ownership_boundary: No provider credential, Daraja configuration, raw callback or secret value is ever surfaced in Servana.

entries.title: Refer & Earn Qualification Decisions
entries.blocked_by: Phase 21R-B, which Plan §80.1 makes dependent on Phase 20D-W, which is behind External Gate W
entries.entry_condition: External Gate W opens, Phase 20D-W completes, and Phase 21R-B ships the activity-qualification decision run and its reconciliation evidence.
entries.why_no_partial_page: Phase 21R-A delivered referral CAPTURE and signed outbox delivery only. No qualification decision has ever been computed, so there is no decision to review.
entries.ownership_boundary: Citrus Refer & Earn owns reward calculation, the reward ledger and payout. Servana owns only its own activity-qualification decision and never gains a reward mutation.

entries.title: Platform Reports
entries.blocked_by: Phase 21N, which Plan §80.1 makes dependent on Phase 20D-W, which is behind External Gate W
entries.entry_condition: External Gate W opens, Phase 20D-W completes, and Phase 21N ships the reporting catalogue (Plan §69) with a platform-scoped read key. `reports.view` is a merchant-scope key today and is not granted to super_admin.
entries.why_no_partial_page: The contract's report set is majority Wallet-derived — payment success, failure, cancellation, timeout, confirmed-to-applied latency, exception backlog and allocation drift. A report page that silently omitted them would misreport platform revenue and recovery.
entries.ownership_boundary: Revenue is defined from validated, applied financial events; nothing here would infer it from gross issuance.

entries.title: Notifications
entries.blocked_by: Phase 21N, which depends on Phases 17, 18 and 20D-W, and 20D-W is behind External Gate W
entries.entry_condition: External Gate W opens, Phase 20D-W completes, and Phase 21N ships the notification record, delivery channel and acknowledgement state (Plan §66).
entries.why_no_partial_page: No notification record, delivery channel or acknowledgement state exists in the repository. The existing notificationStore is a client-side toast queue, not an inbox — the header control keeps its toast behaviour and claims no inbox.
entries.ownership_boundary: Notification content would be redacted and permission-scoped; nothing is subscribed or unsubscribed by the Account and Security page while the runtime is off.
entries.gate_identifier_amendment_reason: 7A minted phase_21n_blocked_by_external_gate_w so the transitive blocker was visible in the identifier itself. Increment 7B collapsed it back to the single external_gate_w vocabulary the readiness matrix, the generated registry and Ui07NavigationContractTest all speak, because two identifiers for one gate is a second vocabulary that can drift. The transitive fact is not lost: blocking_kind stays "transitive", blocked_by names Phase 21N and its dependency chain, and the runtime reason appends backend_owner_phase so the user reads "External Gate W — Wallet by Citrus collections readiness (Phase 21N)".
